# Copilot Instructions — Tiny Tool Town

## Project Overview

Tiny Tool Town is a community-driven directory website for free, open-source tiny tools, built with [Astro](https://astro.build) and deployed as a static site to GitHub Pages. Tools are submitted via GitHub Issues (directly, or through the external [TinyToolSubmitter](https://github.com/jamesmontemagno/TinyToolSubmitter) CLI, which opens an issue for you), automatically converted to markdown content files, and rendered into the site.

## Build & Run

```bash
npm ci             # Install exact dependencies (CI standard; Node 24)
npm run dev        # Local dev server
npm run build      # Production build (outputs to dist/)
npm run preview    # Preview production build locally
npm test           # Run the Vitest test suite
npm run social     # (Re)generate static social cards into public/social/
```

Tests live in `src/lib/__tests__/` and run with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev) (`npm test`). There is no linter configured. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `npm ci`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` on every pull request. Workflows standardize on **Node 24** and `npm ci`.

## Architecture

- **Content-driven static site**: Tools are Astro content collections. Each tool is a markdown file in `src/content/tools/` with YAML frontmatter. The schema is defined in `src/content.config.ts` using Zod.
- **Submission pipeline (queue → batch import)**: Users submit via a GitHub Issue form → `triage-tool.yml` runs automated checks and labels the issue (`ready-to-approve`, `needs-attention`, `duplicate`, etc.) → a maintainer labels it `approved` → `approve-tool.yml` adds the `queued-import` label and dispatches `batch-approve.yml` → `batch-approve.yml` parses queued issues, writes the tool `.md` file(s), downloads thumbnails, generates social cards, commits to `main`, and triggers a deploy.
- **Shared issue-form parser**: `scripts/issue-form-parser.cjs` is the single source of truth for parsing the submission issue form. Both `triage-tool.yml` and `batch-approve.yml` `require` it (via `actions/github-script`), and it is unit-tested in `src/lib/__tests__/issue-form-parser.test.ts`. It also exposes `normalizeRepoFromUrl()` for duplicate detection.
- **Duplicate detection**: Triage and batch import both normalize each submission's `github_url` and compare against existing tool files. Triage labels duplicates `needs-attention` + `duplicate` and comments; batch import refuses to write a second page for an already-listed repo.
- **Thumbnails**: Stored in `public/thumbnails/`. The import workflow and `scripts/fetch-thumbnails.mjs` both extract the largest non-badge image from a tool's README.
- **Social cards (Open Graph images)**: Rendering logic lives in `scripts/social-card.mjs` (`renderSocialCard` for tools, `renderAuthorSocialCard` for authors); `scripts/generate-social.mjs` (run via `npm run social`) writes static `public/social/{slug}.png` files for tools and `public/social/authors/{github}.png` files for authors, both **incrementally** (only new/changed entries). Author cards are self-contained (no network/avatar fetch) and built from existing tool data — display name, handle, tool count, tags, languages. A normal `astro build` no longer prerenders hundreds of images. `src/pages/tools/[slug].astro` references `/social/{slug}.png` and `src/pages/authors/[github].astro` references `/social/authors/{github}.png` when the file exists, otherwise both fall back to the default `/og-image.png`. Deploy workflows run `npm run social` before building; the import workflow generates cards for newly imported tools.
- **Sitemap**: Generated at build time by `@astrojs/sitemap` (configured in `astro.config.mjs`).
- **AI summaries**: `generate-summaries.yml` reads each tool's README via the GitHub API, sends it to the Copilot SDK (with prompt-injection hardening), and writes `ai_summary` and `ai_features` fields into the frontmatter. These render on detail pages in a purple "Copilot says" card.

## Key Conventions

### Tool Markdown Files (`src/content/tools/*.md`)

Every tool file follows this frontmatter schema (see `src/content.config.ts`):

```yaml
---
name: "Tool Name"
tagline: "One-line description"
author: "Author Name"
author_github: "github-username"
github_url: "https://github.com/owner/repo"
website_url: "https://optional.com"        # optional
thumbnail: "/thumbnails/tool-name.png"     # optional
tags: ["cli", "fun"]                       # max 5, lowercase
language: "Python"                         # optional
license: "MIT"                             # optional
date_added: "2026-02-09"
featured: false
ai_summary: "..."                          # optional, generated by TinyToolSummarizer
ai_features: ["...", "..."]                # optional, generated by TinyToolSummarizer
---

Description in markdown body.
```

- The filename (slug) is derived from the tool name: lowercase, alphanumeric + hyphens only.
- Tags go through synonym normalization (e.g., `devtools` → `developer-tools`) and language names are excluded from tags.
- `ai_summary` and `ai_features` should not be manually written; they are generated by the summarizer workflow.
- `thumbnail_source` (optional) records the original upstream image URL; `thumbnail` is the local optimized copy under `/thumbnails/`.

### Astro Components

- All pages use `BaseLayout.astro` and include `Header.astro` / `Footer.astro`.
- Styles are scoped per-component using `<style>` blocks (Astro's default). Global styles are in `src/styles/global.css`.
- CSS uses custom properties prefixed `--color-*` and `--radius*` defined in global.css.
- The `langColors` record mapping language names to dot colors is duplicated in `ToolCard.astro` and `[slug].astro` — keep them in sync.

### GitHub Actions Workflows

- `ci.yml` — Runs `npm ci`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` on every pull request (and `workflow_dispatch`).
- `deploy.yml` — Builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to `main`. Refreshes star counts and generates social cards before building.
- `triage-tool.yml` — On new/edited submission issues: runs automated checks, detects duplicates, and applies triage labels.
- `approve-tool.yml` — Triggered when an issue is labeled `approved`. Adds `queued-import` and dispatches the batch importer.
- `batch-approve.yml` — Processes the `queued-import` queue: parses issues (shared parser), refuses duplicates, writes tool `.md` files, fetches thumbnails, generates social cards, commits to `main`, and triggers a deploy. Runs on the `approved`-label dispatch with an hourly scheduled fallback.
- `generate-summaries.yml` — Generates AI summaries/features for tools (prompt-injection hardened).
- `refresh-thumbnails.yml` — Re-fetches thumbnails from READMEs and regenerates affected social cards.
- `refresh-stars.yml` — Refreshes the GitHub star-count cache and redeploys.
- `refresh-featured-tools.yml` — Rotates the featured-tools selection via PR.
